Add no other exception. The `enterprise-bootstrap` skill meets that test and keeps its name: it carries Bootstrap 5.3 craft, assumes no stack, and names the `.agents/orchestration.md` and `.claude/rules/quality.md` files only where they are present. Do not rename it into the namespace.\r\n- Keep `SKILL.md` concise and route conditional detail to one-level `references/`.\r\n- Name every Markdown file in a skill's `references/` from its `SKILL.md`, and delete a reference nothing names.\r\n- Frontmatter contains only `name` and a trigger-focused `description`.\r\n- Set `name` to the skill's own directory name.\r\n- Write `description` as a single-line scalar or a folded `>-` block, and no other shape. Include in it a sentence beginning `Use ` that names when to invoke the skill.\r\n- Do not put model routing or package version catalogs in a skill.\r\n- Validate every referenced resource, leave no template TODOs, and limit each skill directory to `SKILL.md`, `agents/openai.yaml`, and the `references/*.md` files its `SKILL.md` names; add no other file or directory.\r\n- Write `agents/openai.yaml` as one root `interface:` mapping over exactly `display_name`, `short_description`, and `default_prompt`, in that order, each on its own two-space-indented line.\r\n- Research the external schema only when a consumer needs a key outside `display_name`, `short_description`, and `default_prompt`, and add no key before then.\r\n- Give every one of those keys a non-empty single-quoted scalar, and write an apostrophe inside it as `''`.\r\n- Name the skill's own `$<directory>` token in `default_prompt`.\r\n- Keep provider bridges minimal: they load one canonical workflow and add no competing instructions.\r\n- Give a provider bridge its canonical skill's `name` and `description` verbatim, name the `.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` path it loads, and give it no references of its own.\r\n- Give every canonical skill exactly one provider bridge directory of the same name, and give every bridge directory a canonical twin.\r\n- Review a bridge body's remaining instructions yourself: the policy sweep proves `name` and `description` parity, the named canonical path, and the absence of bridge-owned references, and nothing else about the body.\r\n# Developer-facing writing rules\r\n\r\nThese rules govern prose a developer reads, including chat replies, reports, guides, README files,\r\nand commit messages.\r\n`AGENTS.md` A\u0015 Writing governs prose everywhere, and this file does not restate it; this file adds\r\nonly what a developer audience decides. An instruction file follows `AGENTS.md` A\u0015 Instruction files\r\nfirst, and these rules wherever a rule here names no different form for it.\r\n\r\n## Voice and actor\r\n\r\n- Write `must` for a requirement, `can` for an option or an ability, and `might` for a possibility.\r\n  A recommendation takes the imperative, the same form `AGENTS.md` A\u0015 Writing fixes for instructions.\r\n  Never write `should`, and never soften a recommendation into `We recommend`.\r\n- Address the developer as `you`. Name the software component that acts, and make it the subject of\r\n  the sentence. Reserve `user` for someone using software the developer builds. Never write `we`,\r\n  `our`, or `let's` about agent work.\r\n- Give software no human faculties. A component reports, returns, detects, or refuses; it never\r\n  knows, thinks, wants, or sees.\r\n- Use the passive voice only where naming the actor adds blame and nothing else, such as a defect\r\n  count. Name the actor wherever the reader needs it.\r\n- Use negative contractions (`don't`, `isn't`, `can't`) in a reply or a guide. Do not use them in an\r\n  instruction file.\r\n\r\n## Sentence and paragraph order\r\n\r\n- Put the condition, the goal, or the location before the instruction, so a reader the instruction\r\n  does not apply to stops at the first clause. Put the result or the reason after it. This governs a\r\n  sentence, not a document: a report still opens with its finding.\r\n- Put the key point in the first sentence of every paragraph and every list item, not only in the\r\n  opening of the reply or the section.\r\n- Keep the helper words `that`, `then`, `of`, `a`, and `the`. Do not drop one for brevity.\r\n- Name the noun after `this`, `these`, or `it` wherever the reader could attach the pronoun to\r\n  another referent.\r\n- State what the reader can do. Do not write a double negative.\r\n\r\n## Claims and time\r\n\r\n- Claim only what the reader can check. Never write `ensure`, `guarantee`, a superlative, or an\r\n  effort adjective as a claim about behavior, and cite the run behind every number. `ensure`\r\n  addressed to an executor as a directive is outside this ban.\r\n- Write the present tense for what exists. Do not write `currently`, `now`, `new`, `latest`, or\r\n  `soon`; where time matters, give the version or the date.\r\n- Recommend one path, the shortest one you proved. Rule on every option you list, and drop an option\r\n  equivalent to the one you recommend.\r\n\r\n## Code tokens, references, and links\r\n\r\n- Put a code token in backticks and follow it with a noun: the `parse` method, the `vite.config.ts`\r\n  file, the `--check` flag. Never inflect, pluralize, or possessivize a code token, and never use one\r\n  as an English verb.\r\n- Point to other material with `preceding`, `following`, `earlier`, or `later`, never with `above` or\r\n  `below`. Use `earlier` and `later` for a version range too.\r\n- Write link text as the destination's title or a descriptive phrase, introduced by `see`. Never\r\n  write `here`, `this document`, or a bare URL in prose.\r\n- Paraphrase third-party content and link its source; never paste it into prose you author. A\r\n  vendored mirror is fetched bytes rather than authored prose, and `.claude/rules/documentation.md`\r\n  governs it.\r\n\r\n## Structure\r\n\r\n- Keep a required fact in the main flow. A note or a notice carries only what the reader can skip,\r\n  never a prerequisite, a step, or a warning the task depends on.\r\n- In a reply or a guide, introduce every list, table, and code fence with a complete sentence naming\r\n  what follows; a rule file's list sits bare under its heading. Number a list only where order or\r\n  rank matters. Use a table only for rows with comparable fields.\r\n- Write a heading in sentence case, verb first for a task and a noun phrase for a concept. Identity\r\n  numbering �?\" a claim, an audit verdict, a plan unit �?\" is data rather than a heading style, and\r\n  stays.\r\n\r\n## Examples, numbers, and abbreviations\r\n\r\n- Build an example from fictional data with descriptive names and no personally identifiable\r\n  information. Write a placeholder in `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE` and explain it on first use. Never write\r\n  `foo`, `bar`, or `baz`.\r\n- Expand an abbreviation the reader may not know on first use, with the short form in parentheses.\r\n  Skip the expansion for one this audience reads daily, such as `API`, `CLI`, `JSON`, `URL`, or a\r\n  file format.\r\n- Write a numeral for a technical quantity, a version, or a measurement. Write a date as\r\n  `YYYY-MM-DD` in evidence, commit messages, and reports. See `AGENTS.md` A\u0015 Writing for what\r\n  separates a value from a count.\r\n- Use the serial comma. Mark omitted code with a comment in the sample's language, never with `...`.\r\n\r\n## Substitutions\r\n\r\nReplace each term in this table with its replacement. A literal code identifier is data, and so is\r\na sample string inside a code fence or a test fixture: quote each as itself, exempt from every row.\r\n\r\n| Term                     | Replacement                               |\r\n| ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------- |\r\n| `should`                 | `must`, `can`, `might`, or the imperative |\r\n| `simply`, `easy`, `just` | Delete                                    |\r\n| `currently`, `now`       | Delete, or give the date                  |\r\n| `new`, `latest`          | Delete, or give the version               |\r\n| `utilize`, `leverage`    | `use`                                     |\r\n| `via`                    | `through`, `by using`                     |\r\n| `in order to`            | `to`                                      |\r\n| `e.g.`, `i.e.`           | `for example`, `that is`                  |\r\n| `etc.`                   | Bound the list, or recast the sentence    |\r\n| `performant`, `robust`   | The measured property                     |\r\n| `allows you to`          | `lets you`                                |\r\n| `and/or`                 | `and`, `or`, or `both`                    |\r\n| `since` (causal)         | `because`                                 |\r\n| `once` (temporal)        | `after`                                   |\r\n| `please`                 | Delete                                    |\r\n| `sanity check`           | `quick check`                             |\r\n| `dummy`                  | `placeholder`                             |\r\n| `blacklist`, `whitelist` | `denylist`, `allowlist`                   |\r\n| `master`, `slave`        | `primary`, `replica`                      |\r\n\r\n- `policy/no-banned-term` reads every comment and the prose sweep in `tests/setupPolicy.ts` reads\r\n  every authored Markdown file, and each matches the rows this table bans unconditionally. The rule\r\n  and the sweep leave `now`, `new`, `latest`, `once`, `since`, and `master` unmatched because those\r\n  rows carry a permitted sense, so rule a hit in one of those rows yourself.\r\n- Sweep case-insensitively and across inflections when checking prose against the preceding table. A\r\n  pattern for `easy` reaches neither `Easy` nor `easier`, and a temporal `once` most often appears\r\n  as a sentence-initial `Once`.\r\n- Rule every hit by the sense its row bans, not by the match. `once` counts as often as it means\r\n  `after`, and `new` names a value as often as it dates one. Record a hit in a permitted sense as\r\n  permitted rather than dropping it.\r\n- Name the pattern and the paths behind every sweep result, including a clean one. A result naming\r\n  neither reports on the population its pattern admitted rather than on the population it was drawn\r\n  from.\r\n- Write singular `they` for a person of unstated gender.\r\n- This table carries no row for `execute`, `abort`, `kill`, `terminate`, or `run`:\r\n  `.claude/rules/names.md` A\u0015 Fixed lifecycle vocabulary owns those words, and no row here overrides\r\n  it.\r\n\r\n## Not adopted\r\n\r\n- Do not add conversational personality, warmth, or memorability to a reply; the prose stays plain.\r\n- Do not import a license to break these rules where a departure reads better; an exception exists\r\n  only where a rule states it.\r\n- `We recommend` as a recommendation form �?\" refused in A\u0015 Voice and actor.\r\n- Do not apply a source guide's sample indentation or line-length chrome; the repository formatter\r\n  and `.claude/rules/typescript.md` decide code presentation.\r\n- Do not write an unspaced em dash; this project spaces it.\r\n- Do not cap a sentence at a word count; `AGENTS.md` A\u0015 Writing owns sentence length.\r\n- Do not treat an external word list as vocabulary law; the preceding substitution table is the\r\n  adopted set.\r\n---\r\npaths:\r\n  - 'tests/**/*'\r\n  - 'vite.config.ts'\r\n  - 'configs/**/*.ts'\r\n  - 'package.json'\r\n---\r\n\r\n# Testing rules\r\n\r\n## Test contract\r\n\r\n- Mirror module/application structure:\r\n  `tests/{src,app}/[environment]/[domain]/[module].test.ts`.\r\n- The mirrored population is `src` and `app` alone. `configs/` is a source directory and is\r\n  deliberately not a mirrored root: its leaves produce the workspace's configuration rather than ship\r\n  in it, and they are proved from `tests/config.test.ts` beside the configuration they produce. Do\r\n  not add `tests/configs/`.\r\n- Resolve a mirrored module through `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.mts`, `.cts`, `.vue`, `.scss`, or `.css`.\r\n- Resolve a Sass or CSS partial through the module's leading underscore.\r\n- Resolve each root `tests/setup*.test.ts` proof against its sibling `tests/setup*.ts` module. A\r\n  root `tests/setup.test.ts` file can prove several setup modules when their helpers serve\r\n  several projects.\r\n- Prefer test filenames matching entrypoints: `index.test.ts` for `index.ts`, `main.test.ts` for `main.ts`.\r\n- Tests are deterministic: identical inputs produce identical results.\r\n- Keep default suites fast: timers normally use 10�?\"50 ms and tests make no network calls.\r\n- Use real implementations and small scenarios. Never use mocks, behavioral fakes, module replacement, or framework spies for project-owned or integrated behavior.\r\n- Use recorders for calls/events, temporary resources for stateful boundaries, protocol-faithful fixture servers for deterministic network peers, and the real external service when its behavior is the claim.\r\n- Prefer inert customizable data and input stubs.\r\n- Allow a scripted boundary stub only when it implements the real interface or protocol minimally, to drive the system under test. It never reimplements project-owned behavior and never stands in for the integration being claimed.\r\n- Bind a test fixture server to `127.0.0.1` on an ephemeral port (`listen(0)`), never to `::1` and never to a fixed port: a host without IPv6 fails `EAFNOSUPPORT`, and a fixed port flakes on occupancy.\r\n- Cover happy paths, error paths, empty input, boundary values, `NaN`, positive/negative zero, cycles, and Map/Set order where relevant.\r\n- Test observable behavior, not implementation details.\r\n- Assert the membership a discovered or globbed set must have, not a total that a partly empty population satisfies. A glob spanning two locations passes a size check while one of them matches nothing.\r\n- Never assert an implementation against itself. Compare the answer to a declaration, a fixture, or a second mechanism that could disagree with it. Re-deriving the answer the same way the source derives it produces a test that passes for every value the source ever returns, and it reads exactly like a real one.\r\n- Probe a host-varying property at runtime, on the host the test is running on, and assert against what the probe returned. Filesystem case folding, path separators, permission bits, and rename semantics differ per host, so a fixture built on one host describes that host and silently measures something else on the next.\r\n- Assert a runtime-chosen result as the property it must have, not as the number one run produced. Compression, timing, and buffer sizing are the runtime's choice, so pin the relationship the test depends on �?\" that the encoded form is larger, that the second call is faster �?\" and let the assertion fail when the input drifts out of the range where that relationship holds.\r\n- Measure an elapsed interval with `performance.now()`, never `Date.now()`. `Date.now()` returns whole milliseconds, so an interval built from two of its readings truncates at both ends and can under-report by a millisecond �?\" enough to fail a boundary assertion against a timer that behaved correctly. `performance.now()` is monotonic and sub-millisecond, and it does not move when the wall clock does.\r\n- Give a conditional skip the mechanism that makes it inapplicable, cited, not the platform name alone. A test skipped on a platform is a test nobody re-examines; a test skipped because a named API rejects a named case is one anybody can re-check.\r\n- A regression test records the exact command and its failing count before the fix, and the same command's passing count after.\r\n- The revert that proves a repair reddens exactly the test that names the defect. Keep the import and collection graph valid while reverting, and confirm the named test was collected. A revert that reddens anything beyond that test broke the harness, and its count is not evidence.\r\n- Use `it.todo()` only for explicitly out-of-scope roadmap work, never to complete the current request. Every `.skip` or conditional skip has a narrow verifiable applicability reason.\r\n- Do not create test files solely for `constants.ts`, barrels, error definitions, or `types.ts`.\r\n- Run the narrowest relevant Vitest project during development; do not run the entire suite casually.\r\n\r\n## Cross-cutting proofs\r\n\r\nA proof that covers the workspace instead of one module has a fixed location, so no package invents\r\nits own:\r\n\r\n| Path                         | Proves                                                                                                                                                                                       |\r\n| ---------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\r\n| `tests/policy.test.ts`       | The path- and text-shaped policy laws: mirrors, suppressions, the rule map, filenames, manifest scripts, skills, and bridges                                                                 |\r\n| `tests/config.test.ts`       | Root configuration resolves its aliases, projects, and outputs, and the `configs/` leaves behind them                                                                                        |\r\n| `tests/guides.test.ts`       | Every documented API exists, every public API is documented, every compared summary, example, and pitch equals its source, and every executable fence returns what the guide says it returns |\r\n| `tests/conformance.test.ts`  | Where this package drifts from the official tooling it tracks                                                                                                                                |\r\n| `tests/distribution.test.ts` | The packed package installs and resolves through its public exports                                                                                                                          |\r\n| `tests/integration.test.ts`  | The package's features work together end to end across environments                                                                                                                          |\r\n| `tests/setup*.test.ts`       | Reusable behavior exported from sibling `tests/setup*.ts` modules works as the workspace's suites require                                                                                    |\r\n| `tests/service/**/*.test.ts` | The live external services this package drives, driven for real                                                                                                                              |\r\n\r\n- Put each root `tests/setup*.test.ts` proof in the `setup` project. Keep its assertions on\r\n  exported test-infrastructure behavior: do not duplicate production behavior there, and do not\r\n  move setup-helper assertions into another cross-cutting proof.\r\n- `.claude/rules/workspace.md` names the Vitest project each location belongs to.\r\n- The `guides` project runs in Node with the browser disabled. Its subject is what the guide\r\n  claims: that every documented name resolves, and that every fence asserting a value returns\r\n  that value. A proof that renders a component and compares it against a definition is a\r\n  composition and belongs in an `integration.test.ts` scoped to its directory.\r\n- Transcribe each flagship fence and assert the values its comments claim. Name resolution is\r\n  not a behavioural proof, so a fence documenting a value the code contradicts passes every\r\n  parity assertion. Change a fence, change the transcription beside it.\r\n- `integration.test.ts` is a reserved filename at any level. It names a scope rather than a module,\r\n  so the mirror rule does not reach it; its scope is the directory it sits in.\r\n- An integration test is an end-to-end test: it composes the package's own features and drives them\r\n  together, through the public API, with no part of the system under test replaced.\r\n- Scope it by where the composition happens. `tests/integration.test.ts` drives features **across**\r\n  environments �?\" core through server, core through browser, one environment's output consumed by\r\n  another. A nested `tests/src/<environment>/integration.test.ts` drives features **within** that one\r\n  environment.\r\n- Do not put a packaging, install, or distribution check in an integration test. What the tarball\r\n  contains is a different question from whether the features compose.\r\n- A test the mirror rule flags is a misplaced test until its placement is checked. Move it to the\r\n  location its scope names. Widen the rule only when that check shows the test already sits at the\r\n  location its scope names and the rule's population omits a module this ruleset mandates, and then\r\n  widen the population rather than admitting the individual case.\r\n- A nested `tests/{src,app}/<environment>/**/integration.test.ts` runs in that environment's project,\r\n  whose existing glob collects it exactly once. Give it a separate exact-path project entry only when\r\n  the proof needs different setup or a different runtime, and exclude that exact path from the\r\n  environment project when you do.\r\n\r\n## Probes\r\n\r\nA probe is a throwaway instrument that settles one question. It is not a test and never ships.\r\n\r\nRoute the question before writing a probe. When you can state the edit you believe is correct and the\r\nedit that must break with the stage it breaks at, the question is a claim for the `prove` tool the\r\n`probe` MCP server registers, and `.claude/rules/quality.md` A\u0015 Instruments owns that rule. When the\r\nquestion carries no stated belief to falsify yet, when the subject lies outside the TypeScript a\r\nworkspace project judges, or when the proof needs what that tool's stages do not model �?\" a process\r\ntree, a listening socket, an installed package, a built entry driven as a child, or a live external\r\nservice �?\" write a probe.\r\n\r\nThe kinds split by which tool has to see the probe:\r\n\r\n- A **type probe** is read by `tsc`, whose scoped project includes only its own environment, so it\r\n  lives in the source tree beside what it measures. Delete it before the unit returns; a leaked one\r\n  fails the `policy` plugin's placement rules, because a probe filename is not a centralized kind\r\n  file.\r\n- A **runtime probe** is collected by a Vitest project, so it lives in `tmp/probe/` and runs through\r\n  the `probe` project. `tmp/` is ignored by git, so no probe enters a commit by accident, and every\r\n  test script names its project, so no gate runs the `probe` project.\r\n- A **bench** is read by Vitest's benchmark mode, so it lives inside a test file as a block behind\r\n  the `if (import.meta.env.MODE === 'benchmark')` guard. Only the `test:bench` script collects the\r\n  block, test mode fails an unguarded `bench()` call loudly, and no gate runs a bench. Call `bench`\r\n  directly inside the guard. A `describe` inside it trips `vitest/no-conditional-tests`, and a suite\r\n  the guard leaves unregistered fails test mode with `No test found in suite`.\r\n\r\nRun a probe before relying on an unverified belief about behaviour: what a function returns, what a\r\nconfiguration resolves to, whether a path is reached at all. Prefer a probe to an argument whenever\r\nthe probe is cheap.\r\n\r\nWhen the question is whether the difference between methods is a magnitude or negligible, write a\r\nguarded bench block beside the probe test and run the `test:bench` script. Declare the threshold\r\nbefore the run, read the ratio between the methods against each side's reported uncertainty, and\r\nrecord nothing below a magnitude. A settled magnitude that underwrites an implementation choice\r\npromotes with its test into the mirrored suite and keeps its guarded block there while that choice\r\nstands. A deterministic relationship promotes as an ordinary assertion, so delete the block. Never\r\ncommit baseline output.\r\n\r\nThese rules bind every probe:\r\n\r\n- **Prove the instrument can fail before trusting that it passed.** Pair it with a control drawn\r\n  from outside the population it covers.\r\n- **Promote or delete.** A probe that settles a claim becomes a test in the mirrored location that\r\n  proves the real source. Delete every other probe. A probe left in the suite reports on the harness\r\n  while reading as a test.\r\n- **Never commit a probe.** The ignore rule stops an accident, not a deliberate forced add, and a\r\n  type probe sits in tracked source with no ignore rule at all.\r\n\r\n## Live-service tests\r\n\r\nLive external services/models are the deliberate exception to fast hermetic defaults:\r\n\r\n- Put them in the `service` project, under `tests/service/`, with `tests/setupService.ts` for setup\r\n  and a longer timeout. That module's presence is what registers the project, so a live proof with\r\n  no readiness setup is a project nothing configures.\r\n- `.claude/rules/workspace.md` fixes which gate runs the `service` project, and that gate is not the\r\n  same one in a publishing and a `private: true` workspace.\r\n- Warm and verify service readiness in `tests/setupService.ts`.\r\n- Hard-require readiness: throw loudly; never silently skip.\r\n- Verify service-dependent logic through that service's project, not unrelated module tests or scattered conditional skips.\r\n- Tune each request to the smallest input/context/output that proves one behavior without becoming brittle or expensive.\r\n- Prefer semantic bounded assertions over exact generated prose. Increase context/workload only when the scenario requires it.\r\n\r\n## Expensive proofs\r\n\r\nA test that spawns a process, packs, installs, or drives a real build is a proof, not a unit test.\r\n\r\n- Give it its own Vitest project with its own setup and timeout.\r\n- Keep it out of the default run where the workspace has a gate that can hold it.\r\n  `.claude/rules/workspace.md` fixes which gate each isolated project runs from, and that placement\r\n  differs between a publishing and a `private: true` workspace.\r\n- The fixed expensive-proof projects are `distribution` and `service`.\r\n- A `distribution` proof reads `import.meta.env.MODE` and fails, rather than skips, on an unreachable\r\n  registry under `--mode release`. The publish gate invokes it that way, so a proof that skips there\r\n  passes the gate without ever proving the artifact installs. An ordinary local run may still skip.\r\n- Slow and hermetic is reason enough to isolate a proof; it need not touch an external service.\r\n- Where such a proof stays in a shared project, size its budget from a full contended run rather than from an isolated one. A budget that clears the isolated cost by a thin margin turns contention into a red gate reporting a timeout, which carries no diagnostic about the code and costs a full investigation to dismiss.\r\n\r\n## Shared test infrastructure\r\n\r\nTest helpers are shared infrastructure, not local test-file clutter.\r\n\r\n`@orkestrel/test` owns the helpers every workspace repeats: the call recorder, the real delay, the JSON and async collectors, and the owned scratch directory. Import them from `@orkestrel/test`, and its Node-only helpers from `@orkestrel/test/server`. Write a helper of your own only where the package exports none for the job. The following shapes are the contract a workspace codes against, not source to copy.\r\n\r\n- For the vendored test set (`tests/setupPolicy.ts`, `tests/policy.test.ts`, and\r\n  `tests/config.test.ts`), keep shared helpers within that set instead of importing them from\r\n  `@orkestrel/test`; follow the vendored-file import law in `.claude/rules/workspace.md`.\r\n\r\n- Extract a fixture, recorder, event factory, async wait, renderer, scenario/data builder, protocol fixture, or DOM builder as soon as it could serve another test.\r\n- Any duplicate or near-duplicate helper is a defect; consolidate it into one general form.\r\n- Export every reusable helper, fixture type, factory, constant, and guard from setup files.\r\n- A setup file owns everything an assertion needs and nothing an assertion is: `describe`, `it`, and `expect` never appear in a `setup*.ts`.\r\n- Data tables and case matrices belong in a setup file at any size; test registration does not.\r\n- Test files import shared infrastructure rather than declaring local fixture factories.\r\n- Never reimplement a framework helper in tests or fixtures; import the real parser, signer, flattener, or other helper.\r\n- Prefer small customizable factories/stubs that seed inert data for a real scenario over repeated inline setup.\r\n- Helper names follow module-helper naming: `createFixtureServer`, `buildElement`, `appendItems`, `renderRows`, `waitForReady`, `extractDetail`.\r\n\r\nPlace helpers by environment:\r\n\r\n- `tests/setup.ts`: host-independent; no `node:*`, DOM, `window`, or Vue.\r\n- `tests/setupServer.ts`: Node-only helpers and `node:fs` loaders anchored to `WORKSPACE_ROOT`.\r\n- `tests/setupBrowser.ts`: DOM/Vue/browser helpers and setup CSS.\r\n- `tests/setupStyles.ts`: CSS/style helpers and compiled cascade.\r\n\r\n### Recorder\r\n\r\nImport `createRecorder` from `@orkestrel/test` instead of a framework spy when only calls and arguments matter. It returns:\r\n\r\n```ts\r\ninterface RecorderInterface<TArgs extends readonly unknown[]> {\r\n\treadonly calls: readonly TArgs[]\r\n\treadonly count: number\r\n\treadonly handler: (...args: TArgs) => void\r\n\tclear(): void\r\n}\r\n```\r\n\r\n### Delay\r\n\r\nImport `waitForDelay` from `@orkestrel/test`; never repeat an inline timeout promise. It waits for one host timer and defaults to `0`:\r\n\r\n```ts\r\nfunction waitForDelay(ms?: number): Promise<void>\r\n```\r\n\r\nUse it to yield, never to wait for something another process produces. A fixed delay chosen to\r\noutlast a child's startup is a race whose loss looks like a product defect: the test measures\r\ninterpreter bootstrap rather than the behaviour it names, and it fails on a loaded host and passes on\r\nan idle one. A glob spanning two locations passes a size check while one of them matches nothing.\r\n- Never assert an implementation against itself. Compare the answer to a declaration, a fixture, or a second mechanism that could disagree with it. Re-deriving the answer the same way the source derives it produces a test that passes for every value the source ever returns, and it reads exactly like a real one.\r\n- Probe a host-varying property at runtime, on the host the test is running on, and assert against what the probe returned. Filesystem case folding, path separators, permission bits, and rename semantics differ per host, so a fixture built on one host describes that host and silently measures something else on the next.\r\n- Assert a runtime-chosen result as the property it must have, not as the number one run produced. Compression, timing, and buffer sizing are the runtime's choice, so pin the relationship the test depends on �?\" that the encoded form is larger, that the second call is faster �?\" and let the assertion fail when the input drifts out of the range where that relationship holds.\r\n- Measure an elapsed interval with `performance.now()`, never `Date.now()`. `Date.now()` returns whole milliseconds, so an interval built from two of its readings truncates at both ends and can under-report by a millisecond �?\" enough to fail a boundary assertion against a timer that behaved correctly. `performance.now()` is monotonic and sub-millisecond, and it does not move when the wall clock does.\r\n- Give a conditional skip the mechanism that makes it inapplicable, cited, not the platform name alone. A test skipped on a platform is a test nobody re-examines; a test skipped because a named API rejects a named case is one anybody can re-check.\r\n- A regression test records the exact command and its failing count before the fix, and the same command's passing count after.\r\n- The revert that proves a repair reddens exactly the test that names the defect. Keep the import and collection graph valid while reverting, and confirm the named test was collected. A revert that reddens anything beyond that test broke the harness, and its count is not evidence.\r\n- Use `it.todo()` only for explicitly out-of-scope roadmap work, never to complete the current request. Every `.skip` or conditional skip has a narrow verifiable applicability reason.\r\n- Do not create test files solely for `constants.ts`, barrels, error definitions, or `types.ts`.\r\n- Run the narrowest relevant Vitest project during development; do not run the entire suite casually.\r\n\r\n## Cross-cutting proofs\r\n\r\nA proof that covers the workspace instead of one module has a fixed location, so no package invents\r\nits own:\r\n\r\n| Path                         | Proves                                                                                                                                                                                       |\r\n| ---------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\r\n| `tests/policy.test.ts`       | The path- and text-shaped policy laws: mirrors, suppressions, the rule map, filenames, manifest scripts, skills, and bridges                                                                 |\r\n| `tests/config.test.ts`       | Root configuration resolves its aliases, projects, and outputs, and the `configs/` leaves behind them                                                                                        |\r\n| `tests/guides.test.ts`       | Every documented API exists, every public API is documented, every compared summary, example, and pitch equals its source, and every executable fence returns what the guide says it returns |\r\n| `tests/conformance.test.ts`  | Where this package drifts from the official tooling it tracks                                                                                                                                |\r\n| `tests/distribution.test.ts` | The packed package installs and resolves through its public exports                                                                                                                          |\r\n| `tests/integration.test.ts`  | The package's features work together end to end across environments                                                                                                                          |\r\n| `tests/setup*.test.ts`       | Reusable behavior exported from sibling `tests/setup*.ts` modules works as the workspace's suites require                                                                                    |\r\n| `tests/service/**/*.test.ts` | The live external services this package drives, driven for real                                                                                                                              |\r\n\r\n- Put each root `tests/setup*.test.ts` proof in the `setup` project. Keep its assertions on\r\n  exported test-infrastructure behavior: do not duplicate production behavior there, and do not\r\n  move setup-helper assertions into another cross-cutting proof.\r\n- `.claude/rules/workspace.md` names the Vitest project each location belongs to.\r\n- The `guides` project runs in Node with the browser disabled. Its subject is what the guide\r\n  claims: that every documented name resolves, and that every fence asserting a value returns\r\n  that value. A proof that renders a component and compares it against a definition is a\r\n  composition and belongs in an `integration.test.ts` scoped to its directory.\r\n- Transcribe each flagship fence and assert the values its comments claim. Name resolution is\r\n  not a behavioural proof, so a fence documenting a value the code contradicts passes every\r\n  parity assertion. Change a fence, change the transcription beside it.\r\n- `integration.test.ts` is a reserved filename at any level. It names a scope rather than a module,\r\n  so the mirror rule does not reach it; its scope is the directory it sits in.\r\n- An integration test is an end-to-end test: it composes the package's own features and drives them\r\n  together, through the public API, with no part of the system under test replaced.\r\n- Scope it by where the composition happens. `tests/integration.test.ts` drives features **across**\r\n  environments �?\" core through server, core through browser, one environment's output consumed by\r\n  another. A nested `tests/src/<environment>/integration.test.ts` drives features **within** that one\r\n  environment.\r\n- Do not put a packaging, install, or distribution check in an integration test. What the tarball\r\n  contains is a different question from whether the features compose.\r\n- A test the mirror rule flags is a misplaced test until its placement is checked. Move it to the\r\n  location its scope names. Widen the rule only when that check shows the test already sits at the\r\n  location its scope names and the rule's population omits a module this ruleset mandates, and then\r\n  widen the population rather than admitting the individual case.\r\n- A nested `tests/{src,app}/<environment>/**/integration.test.ts` runs in that environment's project,\r\n  whose existing glob collects it exactly once. Give it a separate exact-path project entry only when\r\n  the proof needs different setup or a different runtime, and exclude that exact path from the\r\n  environment project when you do.\r\n\r\n## Probes\r\n\r\nA probe is a throwaway instrument that settles one question. It is not a test and never ships.\r\n\r\nRoute the question before writing a probe. When you can state the edit you believe is correct and the\r\nedit that must break with the stage it breaks at, the question is a claim for the `prove` tool the\r\n`probe` MCP server registers, and `.claude/rules/quality.md` A\u0015 Instruments owns that rule. When the\r\nquestion carries no stated belief to falsify yet, when the subject lies outside the TypeScript a\r\nworkspace project judges, or when the proof needs what that tool's stages do not model �?\" a process\r\ntree, a listening socket, an installed package, a built entry driven as a child, or a live external\r\nservice �?\" write a probe.\r\n\r\nThe kinds split by which tool has to see the probe:\r\n\r\n- A **type probe** is read by `tsc`, whose scoped project includes only its own environment, so it\r\n  lives in the source tree beside what it measures. Delete it before the unit returns; a leaked one\r\n  fails the `policy` plugin's placement rules, because a probe filename is not a centralized kind\r\n  file.\r\n- A **runtime probe** is collected by a Vitest project, so it lives in `tmp/probe/` and runs through\r\n  the `probe` project. `tmp/` is ignored by git, so no probe enters a commit by accident, and every\r\n  test script names its project, so no gate runs the `probe` project.\r\n- A **bench** is read by Vitest's benchmark mode, so it lives inside a test file as a block behind\r\n  the `if (import.meta.env.MODE === 'benchmark')` guard. Only the `test:bench` script collects the\r\n  block, test mode fails an unguarded `bench()` call loudly, and no gate runs a bench. Call `bench`\r\n  directly inside the guard. A `describe` inside it trips `vitest/no-conditional-tests`, and a suite\r\n  the guard leaves unregistered fails test mode with `No test found in suite`.\r\n\r\nRun a probe before relying on an unverified belief about behaviour: what a function returns, what a\r\nconfiguration resolves to, whether a path is reached at all. Prefer a probe to an argument whenever\r\nthe probe is cheap.\r\n\r\nWhen the question is whether the difference between methods is a magnitude or negligible, write a\r\nguarded bench block beside the probe test and run the `test:bench` script. Declare the threshold\r\nbefore the run, read the ratio between the methods against each side's reported uncertainty, and\r\nrecord nothing below a magnitude. A settled magnitude that underwrites an implementation choice\r\npromotes with its test into the mirrored suite and keeps its guarded block there while that choice\r\nstands. A deterministic relationship promotes as an ordinary assertion, so delete the block. Never\r\ncommit baseline output.\r\n\r\nThese rules bind every probe:\r\n\r\n- **Prove the instrument can fail before trusting that it passed.** Pair it with a control drawn\r\n  from outside the population it covers.\r\n- **Promote or delete.** A probe that settles a claim becomes a test in the mirrored location that\r\n  proves the real source. Delete every other probe. A probe left in the suite reports on the harness\r\n  while reading as a test.\r\n- **Never commit a probe.** The ignore rule stops an accident, not a deliberate forced add, and a\r\n  type probe sits in tracked source with no ignore rule at all.\r\n\r\n## Live-service tests\r\n\r\nLive external services/models are the deliberate exception to fast hermetic defaults:\r\n\r\n- Put them in the `service` project, under `tests/service/`, with `tests/setupService.ts` for setup\r\n  and a longer timeout. That module's presence is what registers the project, so a live proof with\r\n  no readiness setup is a project nothing configures.\r\n- `.claude/rules/workspace.md` fixes which gate runs the `service` project, and that gate is not the\r\n  same one in a publishing and a `private: true` workspace.\r\n- Warm and verify service readiness in `tests/setupService.ts`.\r\n- Hard-require readiness: throw loudly; never silently skip.\r\n- Verify service-dependent logic through that service's project, not unrelated module tests or scattered conditional skips.\r\n- Tune each request to the smallest input/context/output that proves one behavior without becoming brittle or expensive.\r\n- Prefer semantic bounded assertions over exact generated prose. Increase context/workload only when the scenario requires it.\r\n\r\n## Expensive proofs\r\n\r\nA test that spawns a process, packs, installs, or drives a real build is a proof, not a unit test.\r\n\r\n- Give it its own Vitest project with its own setup and timeout.\r\n- Keep it out of the default run where the workspace has a gate that can hold it.\r\n  `.claude/rules/workspace.md` fixes which gate each isolated project runs from, and that placement\r\n  differs between a publishing and a `private: true` workspace.\r\n- The fixed expensive-proof projects are `distribution` and `service`.\r\n- A `distribution` proof reads `import.meta.env.MODE` and fails, rather than skips, on an unreachable\r\n  registry under `--mode release`. The publish gate invokes it that way, so a proof that skips there\r\n  passes the gate without ever proving the artifact installs. An ordinary local run may still skip.\r\n- Slow and hermetic is reason enough to isolate a proof; it need not touch an external service.\r\n- Where such a proof stays in a shared project, size its budget from a full contended run rather than from an isolated one. A budget that clears the isolated cost by a thin margin turns contention into a red gate reporting a timeout, which carries no diagnostic about the code and costs a full investigation to dismiss.\r\n\r\n## Shared test infrastructure\r\n\r\nTest helpers are shared infrastructure, not local test-file clutter.\r\n\r\n`@orkestrel/test` owns the helpers every workspace repeats: the call recorder, the real delay, the JSON and async collectors, and the owned scratch directory. Import them from `@orkestrel/test`, and its Node-only helpers from `@orkestrel/test/server`. Write a helper of your own only where the package exports none for the job. The following shapes are the contract a workspace codes against, not source to copy.\r\n\r\n- For the vendored test set (`tests/setupPolicy.ts`, `tests/policy.test.ts`, and\r\n  `tests/config.test.ts`), keep shared helpers within that set instead of importing them from\r\n  `@orkestrel/test`; follow the vendored-file import law in `.claude/rules/workspace.md`.\r\n\r\n- Extract a fixture, recorder, event factory, async wait, renderer, scenario/data builder, protocol fixture, or DOM builder as soon as it could serve another test.\r\n- Any duplicate or near-duplicate helper is a defect; consolidate it into one general form.\r\n- Export every reusable helper, fixture type, factory, constant, and guard from setup files.\r\n- A setup file owns everything an assertion needs and nothing an assertion is: `describe`, `it`, and `expect` never appear in a `setup*.ts`.\r\n- Data tables and case matrices belong in a setup file at any size; test registration does not.\r\n- Test files import shared infrastructure rather than declaring local fixture factories.\r\n- Never reimplement a framework helper in tests or fixtures; import the real parser, signer, flattener, or other helper.\r\n- Prefer small customizable factories/stubs that seed inert data for a real scenario over repeated inline setup.\r\n- Helper names follow module-helper naming: `createFixtureServer`, `buildElement`, `appendItems`, `renderRows`, `waitForReady`, `extractDetail`.\r\n\r\nPlace helpers by environment:\r\n\r\n- `tests/setup.ts`: host-independent; no `node:*`, DOM, `window`, or Vue.\r\n- `tests/setupServer.ts`: Node-only helpers and `node:fs` loaders anchored to `WORKSPACE_ROOT`.\r\n- `tests/setupBrowser.ts`: DOM/Vue/browser helpers and setup CSS.\r\n- `tests/setupStyles.ts`: CSS/style helpers and compiled cascade.\r\n\r\n### Recorder\r\n\r\nImport `createRecorder` from `@orkestrel/test` instead of a framework spy when only calls and arguments matter. It returns:\r\n\r\n```ts\r\ninterface RecorderInterface<TArgs extends readonly unknown[]> {\r\n\treadonly calls: readonly TArgs[]\r\n\treadonly count: number\r\n\treadonly handler: (...args: TArgs) => void\r\n\tclear(): void\r\n}\r\n```\r\n\r\n### Delay\r\n\r\nImport `waitForDelay` from `@orkestrel/test`; never repeat an inline timeout promise. It waits for one host timer and defaults to `0`:\r\n\r\n```ts\r\nfunction waitForDelay(ms?: number): Promise<void>\r\n```\r\n\r\nUse it to yield, never to wait for something another process produces. A fixed delay chosen to\r\noutlast a child's startup is a race whose loss looks like a product defect: the test measures\r\ninterpreter bootstrap rather than the behaviour it names, and it fails on a loaded host and passes on\r\nan idle one. Wait until a named condition holds instead, polling with `waitForDelay` inside a budget\r\nmeasured by `performance.now()`, and fail with the condition's own description when the budget\r\nexpires.\r\n\r\n### Scratch\r\n\r\nImport `createScratch` from `@orkestrel/test/server` when a proof needs real files. It allocates a temporary directory it owns, contains every path against escape, and removes the directory on `destroy`:\r\n\r\n```ts\r\ninterface ScratchInterface {\r\n\treadonly path: string\r\n\twrite(target: string, text: string): string\r\n\tread(target: string): string | undefined\r\n\thas(target: string): boolean\r\n\tnames(target?: string): readonly string[]\r\n\tensure(target: string): string\r\n\tlink(target: string, source: string): string\r\n\tremove(target: string): void\r\n\tdestroy(): void\r\n}\r\n```\r\n\r\n### Style primitives\r\n\r\nBrowser/style setup exposes shared assertions/builders:\r\n\r\n`mount`, `render`, `build`, `readStyle`, `readToken`, `readRootToken`, `readPixels`, `parseCSSColor`, `matchesColor`, `findRule`.\r\n\r\n`findRule` proves a declaration exists in the cascade; `readStyle()` reads the resolved result.\r\n\r\n## Browser tests\r\n\r\nUse the real browser as the system under test:\r\n\r\n- Do not replace DOM events, storage, observers, viewports, layout methods, pointer, or drag APIs unless the browser genuinely lacks one.\r\n- Prefer real nodes, events, styles/layout, and observers.\r\n- Centralize event factories: `createPointerEvent`, `createDragEvent`, `typeInput`, `fireTransitionEnd`.\r\n- Centralize DOM builders: `createButtonElement`, `createDropdownElements`, `createModalElement`.\r\n- Assert DOM state, emitted events, callback records, focus, classes, attributes, and public API state.\r\n- Do not assert private state, internal timers, or framework scheduler internals.\r\n- Prefer real short timers and observable wakeups. Never replace the host clock.\r\n\r\n## Runner configuration\r\n\r\nKeep Vitest/provider configuration minimal:\r\n\r\n- Prefer defaults until a measured problem proves them insufficient.\r\n- Centralize provider setup in one helper/shared block.\r\n- Add browser/provider/teardown/timeout/parallelism/cache/launch settings only for a current verified need.\r\n- Avoid long browser flag lists and persistent contexts unless a test requires them.\r\n- For slow teardown, inspect test cleanup, open handles, file parallelism, and context churn before adding launch flags.\r\n- Remove exploratory settings after fixing the cause.\r\n- Config comments explain the current reason, not the history of failed experiments.\r\n\r\n## Untestable usually means missing seam\r\n\r\nBefore accepting that a behavior cannot be tested, look for the seam that would make it testable.\r\n\r\n- Treat a collaborator reached through a hard-coded global �?\" a stream, a clock source, a spawn, a fetch �?\" as a missing injection point, not an untestable truth.\r\n- An injected collaborator with a real minimal implementation is a sanctioned boundary stub, not a mock of project-owned behavior.\r\n- Add the seam rather than shipping the gap whenever the design would welcome it anyway, and whenever a sibling collaborator is already injected.\r\n- Record a genuinely irreducible gap where a reader meets it: what is unproven, why it cannot be driven, and what would change that. A silent untested guard reads exactly like a tested one.\r\n\r\nCoverage rules:\r\n\r\n- Read a coverage report as a discovery input, never as evidence of proof. It answers one cheap mechanical question �?\" which code no test executed �?\" and that reliably finds forgotten branches and rules nothing calls.\r\n- Never cite coverage as the adequacy audit's result. It cannot tell you whether an executed line is asserted, so a fully covered file can still be entirely unproven.\r\n- Never let a percentage become the target.\r\n\r\n## Discovery and adequacy audit\r\n\r\nBefore acceptance:\r\n\r\n- prove every intended test file is discovered by the correct project;\r\n- prove every declared project is reachable from a gate. A project registered in the root\r\n  configuration with no script, or with a script no chain runs, is a proof that never executes �?\" and\r\n  because it never executes it never fails, so the suite reports green while carrying it. Read the\r\n  chain, not the exit code: run each project directly once and compare that list against what `test`\r\n  actually invokes. The gate that would report this gap is the gate that is missing.\r\n- prove a declared project's include resolves to a real file. An empty project is not a passing\r\n  project: Vitest exits non-zero on \"no test files found\", so a project aimed at a path that was\r\n  never created stays invisible until something finally runs it.\r\n- inspect actual test counts and environments;\r\n- audit `.todo`, `.skip`, conditional skips, retries, and inflated timeouts;\r\n- confirm each assertion would fail for the defect it claims to catch, and that it fails rather than passes when its population is empty;\r\n- confirm helpers do not reimplement production behavior;\r\n- confirm cleanup runs after setup or assertion failure;\r\n- confirm current-scope requirements have real tests rather than placeholders.\r\n---\r\npaths:\r\n  - '**/*.{ts,tsx,mts,cts,vue}'\r\n---\r\n\r\n# TypeScript rules\r\n\r\nThe non-negotiables and design laws in `AGENTS.md` apply without exception and are not restated here. This file adds only what TypeScript itself decides.\r\n\r\n## Syntax and imports\r\n\r\n- Tabs for indentation.\r\n- No semicolons unless ASI requires one.\r\n- Single quotes.\r\n- Named exports only, except framework-required defaults.\r\n- ESM imports use explicit `.js` extensions for local TypeScript modules.\r\n- Place `import type` declarations before value imports.\r\n- Do not place blank lines between consecutive imports of the same kind.\r\n- Narrow an accepted `unknown` with a total guard rather than a conditional access.\r\n- A parameter property is a constructor parameter carrying any accessibility or `readonly` modifier.\r\n  The ban reaches every form, `readonly` alone included; declare the `#` field and assign it in the\r\n  constructor body.\r\n\r\n## Types\r\n\r\n- Put every reusable or public interface/type alias in the nearest authoritative `*/types.ts`.\r\n- Public collection properties and return types use `readonly T[]`, `ReadonlyMap<K, V>`, or `ReadonlySet<T>`.\r\n- Optional state is `T | undefined`; an optional lookup failure returns `undefined`.\r\n- `as const` annotates a literal with its own type and never overrides the checker, so the assertion\r\n  ban does not reach it. Use it to derive a literal union from a value and to fix a tuple's arity and\r\n  element types. Do not write it on a value whose contract is already declared; annotate the\r\n  declaration instead. A class field that holds one literal keeps `as const`\r\n  (`readonly code = 'ABORT' as const`): the vendored lint gate's `prefer-as-const` rule refuses the\r\n  annotated form, and a field whose type is a union of literals is annotated as the preceding\r\n  sentence states.\r\n\r\n## Immutability\r\n\r\n- Never mutate caller-owned inputs.\r\n- Use copy-on-write for internal state.\r\n- Return copies or readonly views; never leak a mutable internal reference.\r\n- Compute derived facts instead of persisting duplicate state.\r\n\r\n## Errors and outcomes\r\n\r\n| Condition                            | Required strategy                           |\r\n| ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------- |\r\n| Programmer error or invalid argument | Throw an `AppError`                         |\r\n| I/O/network/external operation       | Return `Result<T, E>` or throw consistently |\r\n| Optional missing lookup              | Return `undefined`                          |\r\n| Invalid input inside a guard         | Return `false`; never throw                 |\r\n\r\nUse the existing outcome contract from a declared dependency or the owning environment; do not redeclare it at each call site. When no such contract exists and adding a dependency is not authorized, define this once in the owning `types.ts`:\r\n\r\n```ts\r\ninterface Success<T> {\r\n\treadonly success: true\r\n\treadonly value: T\r\n}\r\n\r\ninterface Failure<E> {\r\n\treadonly success: false\r\n\treadonly error: E\r\n}\r\n\r\ntype Result<T, E = Error> = Success<T> | Failure<E>\r\n```\r\n\r\n- When `@orkestrel/contract` is declared, inspect and use its exact installed `Result`, construction/narrowing helpers, and `attempt` behavior instead of duplicating them.\r\n- Otherwise construct and narrow through the owning environment's centralized helpers.\r\n- Error classes expose a machine-readable `code` and optional `context`.\r\n- Every public error class ships with a guard such as `isAppError` for safe `catch` narrowing.\r\n\r\n## Comments and API documentation\r\n\r\n- Comments explain why, never restate what self-explanatory code does. The Writing rules in `AGENTS.md` and `.claude/rules/writing.md` govern their prose.\r\n- Every public export has complete TSDoc: description, `@param`, `@returns`, and `@example` where applicable.\r\n- The first sentence states what the symbol does in the third person with an `-s` verb �?\" `Creates`,\r\n  `Returns`, `Checks whether` �?\" and never repeats the symbol's name.\r\n- `policy/no-malformed-summary` reads that first sentence over every doc block a top-level export\r\n  declaration follows, and refuses an opening word that is not a third-person `-s` verb and a\r\n  sentence naming the declared symbol. A word ending in `s` that the rule's stop set does not name\r\n  passes whether or not it is a verb �?\" a plural noun such as `Files` included �?\" so read the sentence\r\n  in review as well.\r\n- Describe a boolean parameter as \"If `true`, �?�; if `false`, �?�\", and a boolean return as\r\n  \"True if �?�; false otherwise\".\r\n- Write a default as \"Default: �?�\" and a thrown error as \"Thrown when �?�\".\r\n- State a prerequisite and the failure behavior wherever the symbol has either.\r\n- `@deprecated` names the replacement first, then the reason.\r\n- Document an options object as one `@param`; describe its short fields under `@remarks`.\r\n- Private methods and overload-specific notes use single-line `//` comments, not public TSDoc.\r\n- Do not document speculative future product behavior unless requested.\r\n- Never use `@internal` to hide a method; make it `#` private.\r\n---\r\npaths:\r\n  - 'src/**/*'\r\n  - 'app/**/*'\r\n  - 'tests/**/*'\r\n  - 'guides/**/*'\r\n  - 'package.json'\r\n  - 'vite.config.ts'\r\n  - 'tsconfig.json'\r\n  - '.agents/skills/**/*'\r\n  - '.claude/skills/**/*'\r\n---\r\n\r\n# Research, hardening, and completion rules\r\n\r\n## Evidence before change\r\n\r\n- Research when the user asks for it, when comparing an upstream, protocol, or legacy implementation, or when current external behavior materially affects design.\r\n- Use current primary sources for external capabilities, and the exact installed declarations and guides for dependencies. Separate verified fact from inference.\r\n- Read authoritative types and named decision-bearing implementation files first-hand. Delegate bulk supporting context, never the owning design decision.\r\n- Treat existing code, tests, `old/`, branches, and copied projects as evidence, not authority.\r\n- Build a capability/defect matrix before a broad API or production-readiness change. Every row ends as implement, repair, retain, or intentionally exclude with evidence.\r\n- Fix that matrix when the change starts. It is the definition of done, and the change closes when every row closes.\r\n- Never end a row as \"hardened further.\" Replace any evaluative phrase with the concrete condition that closes the row.\r\n- Record a finding outside the matrix against the row that owns it, for the next matrix. Do not reopen this one.\r\n\r\n## Probes before arguments\r\n\r\nA question a probe can settle is settled by the probe, whether or not anyone has disputed it. Reasoning decides what to run and what the result means. It does not replace the run.\r\n\r\n- Test your own assumptions before you rely on them. You do not need a disagreement to justify a probe. If you are about to depend on what a function returns, what a config resolves to, what a flag does, or whether a path is even reached, run it and find out.\r\n- Treat a long deliberation about behaviour as the signal to stop and run something. Deliberation that a ten-line probe would have ended is the most expensive habit in this process, and it is invisible because it feels like rigour.\r\n- Verify a belief before stating it, or label it as unverified. An unverified assertion put into context becomes a fact for everything downstream, including other agents, and correcting it later costs more than the check would have.\r\n- Hold a claim you issue to the standard you hold a claim you receive. Nothing downstream re-checks an instruction, so an unverified fact inside one becomes the premise of every task built on it. Auditing every report you receive while exempting every brief you write is the common form of this failure.\r\n- Prefer the check over the chain of reasoning whenever the check is cheap. Reading the installed declaration, running one line, or counting the call sites beats three paragraphs inferring the same thing, and it produces evidence you can hand to someone else.\r\n- Write the probe before the argument gets long. The moment a claim about behaviour is disputed �?\" between engines, between a report and a rule, or in your own head �?\" stop and run it. Get the smallest real input through the real code and read the real output.\r\n- Bound the search before starting it, and put the bound in the brief. Name the benchmark, the population, or the row that ends it. An investigation with no stated stopping condition runs until attention runs out. This includes the case where the honest answer is that the limit is inherent and belongs in documentation rather than in code.\r\n- Treat a negative probe as evidence about the probe until its input is shown to reach the code under test. A pass proves nothing if the vector never arrived. Instrument the path, assert an observable side effect, or drive it through a door you can see.\r\n- When a report names a defect and your reproduction comes back clean, assume first that your vector was weaker than theirs, and go get their exact vector. Treating a failed reproduction as a disproof is the most common way a true finding is lost.\r\n- A reported vector the compiler rejects refutes the VECTOR, never the finding. Extend the `AgentProvider` class to reach a new wire, or\r\n`createRelayProvider` and `createRelay` to reach a model through your own server. Callable\r\ntools come from `@orkestrel/tool` and documents from `@orkestrel/workspace`. Part of the\r\n`@orkestrel` line.\r\n\r\n## Install\r\n\r\n```sh\r\nnpm install @orkestrel/agent\r\n```\r\n\r\n## Requirements\r\n\r\n- Node.js >= 22\r\n- Dual ESM + CommonJS builds (`import` and `require` both supported)\r\n\r\n## Usage\r\n\r\n```ts\r\nimport { createAgent } from '@orkestrel/agent'\r\nimport { createTool, createToolManager } from '@orkestrel/tool'\r\n\r\nconst tools = createToolManager()\r\ntools.add(\r\n\tcreateTool({\r\n\t\tname: 'add',\r\n\t\tdescription: 'Add two numbers',\r\n\t\texecute: (args) => Number(args.a) + Number(args.b),\r\n\t}),\r\n)\r\n\r\n// `provider` is your ProviderInterface implementation (see the guide)\r\nconst agent = createAgent(provider, { system: 'You are concise.', tools })\r\nagent.context.messages.add({ role: 'user', content: 'Say hi.' })\r\n\r\nconst stream = agent.stream()\r\nfor await (const chunk of stream.events) {\r\n\tif (chunk.category === 'token') process.stdout.write(chunk.content)\r\n}\r\nconst result = await stream.result // { content, usage?, partial }\r\n```\r\n\r\n## Guide\r\n\r\n[`guides/agent.md`](guides/agent.md) documents the agent-owned surface:\r\nthe provider boundary, the `AgentProvider` HTTP engine, the relay, conversations,\r\ninstructions, scopes, authority, durable jobs, the loop, and `AgentContext`.
